title: The Repair Man (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth trades
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The repair man arrives in a window between eight and twelve
And you clear your whole morning from everything else
Because the window is a window in name only — it's a day
The repair man will be there when the repair man decides to say

[Pre-Chorus]
The repair man has a van and knowledge and a lack of urgency
That I have come to accept as a separate kind of currency

[Chorus]
The repair man knows something I don't know
He knows the fault before he opens anything in the show
The repair man has seen this particular problem forty times before
And the fix takes nine minutes and the quote took ninety more
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
He looks at the thing and he says "there's your problem" and he points
At something I can't see but I trust him at his joints
Of expertise — and the nine minutes happens and it works
And the forty years of knowledge in those nine minutes lurks

[Bridge]
I once tried to fix a tap myself on a Saturday morning
And the tap got worse and I spent four hundred dollars warning
My pride that the repair man exists for very specific reasons
And the reasons are valid across all weeks and seasons

[Outro]
Repair man knows… nine minutes, forty years of knowledge… repair man knows
That's my boy
